post.summary: Search approved Bangladesh statutes for a case
post.description: Hybrid search over the legal knowledge base: e5-large vector search (HNSW, cosine) and 'simple' full-text search fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60), then a reranker (mock by default). Only approved, current statute versions are searched. With `incident_date`, sections not in force on that date are excluded; sections whose status is unknown are included and flagged. Bangla and English versions of the same section are merged and returned as alternates. Results are retrieved sources, not legal conclusions, and are marked unverified. Requires an active lawyer membership in the case. The query text is not logged; an audit event records counts only.

post.summary: Upload and process a case document
post.description: Accepts a PDF, PNG, JPEG, or TIFF of at most 20 MB. The type is checked by magic bytes; password-protected PDFs and oversized images are refused. The original is stored in object storage under cases/{case_id}/documents/{document_id}, then processed synchronously: the PDF text layer is used where present and scanned pages are OCRed with Tesseract (ben+eng), with per-page confidence. Without a malware scanner, development processes the file with scan_status 'not_configured' and a warning; production refuses with NOT_CONFIGURED. Duplicate files in the same case are refused. Requires an active lawyer membership in an open case.

post.summary: Extract draft facts from case documents
post.description: Reads the current text of the case's processed pages (optionally only `document_ids`) and asks the configured extractor for structured facts: parties, dates, places, acts or omissions, documents, relief sought. Page text is sent as untrusted, delimited data. Output must match a JSON schema (validated with Pydantic); an invalid batch is retried once, then the run is marked extraction_failed and nothing is stored. Every quote is checked in code against the exact page version; failed checks are flagged and cannot be confirmed as document_says. All facts are drafts until a lawyer confirms them. Providers: the mock extractor (development and test only) or a local Ollama server; otherwise 503 NOT_CONFIGURED.

post.description: Reads only the confirmed fact set (view case_facts_for_analysis) and records its hash. For each fact it generates search queries and retrieves approved statute text (Step B search, filtered by incident_date). If no provision reaches the relevance threshold it abstains with insufficient_information and lists what is missing. Otherwise it builds element-by-element findings (legal ingredients quoted from the retrieved provision, each mapped to a confirmed fact or marked missing/disputed, strength strong/moderate/weak/insufficient with reasons, statement_type ai_inference). Every citation passes a deterministic verifier (chunk exists, approved, in force or flagged, quote is an NFC substring); failures are stripped or labelled unverified. No precedents are cited unless judgments exist in the knowledge base. Each run is a new immutable version. Requires can_run_ai.

get.description: Returns the newest analysis version for the case.

post.summary: Build a strategy game tree (new version)
post.description: Builds a bounded game tree from the latest (or a given) analysis version: our moves (ply 1, at most 4), opponent or court responses (ply 2, at most 3 per move), our counters (ply 3, at most 3 per response). Every node carries legal_basis citations, requirements, risk/cost/time (low/medium/high/unknown), a strength label and reasons. Each citation must be a provision the analysis retrieved and passes the deterministic verifier; nodes without a verified basis are marked unverified. No percentages. No precedent is cited unless judgments are in the knowledge base (otherwise the precedent_note says so). Each run is a new immutable version. Requires can_run_ai.

post.description: Appends the update to the timeline (order text, notes, next date), adds the order text as a lawyer_entered fact, re-runs the case analysis and the strategy tree on the updated confirmed facts, and returns the reassessment diff: changed findings, closed and new options, tree version, and tasks. A next date creates a confirmed hearing only when the lawyer confirms it; a date found in the order text is a draft suggestion. A plain-language client summary is saved as a draft client update; the client sees it only after the lawyer publishes it. Requires can_run_ai.
